title: Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.02002v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, where many authors record decisions across documents over months. Because a revised decision arrives as a new document rather than an edit, answering a question requires knowing which version held at a given time. However, most memory systems compress the record at write time. By distilling each document into facts, notes or graph edges, these methods fix what can be answered before any question is asked. To address this, we propose Mem++, a non-destructive memory framework shifting from write-time distillation to read-time selection. Mem++ stores every document whole with its date and author, and it calls no generative model at write time. At read time, it retrieves only documents dated up to the time a question asks about and fuses lexical and semantic rankings. Unlike systems that overwrite older versions, Mem++ keeps them and leaves the choice to the answering

translated_title: Mem++：面向长期组织型LLM智能体的非破坏性记忆
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体如今已参与到组织工作中，许多作者会在数月内跨越多份文档记录决策。由于修订后的决策是以新文档的形式到达，而非对原文档的编辑，回答问题需要知道在特定时间点生效的是哪个版本。然而，大多数记忆系统会在写入时压缩记录，通过将每份文档提炼为事实、笔记或图边，这些方法在问题提出之前就固定了可回答的范围。为解决这一问题，我们提出Mem++，一个非破坏性记忆框架，将写入时的提炼转变为读取时的选择。Mem++完整存储每份文档及其日期和作者，并且在写入时不调用任何生成模型。在读取时，它仅检索日期早于问题所询问时间的文档，并融合词法与语义排序。与覆盖旧版本的系统不同，Mem++保留旧版本，并将选择权留给回答环节。
tldr: Mem++提出一种非破坏性记忆框架，完整保存组织文档及其日期和作者信息，将信息处理从写入时的提炼转移到读取时的选择，从而支持针对特定时间点的决策版本问答。
en_tdlr: Mem++ proposes a non-destructive memory framework that stores organizational documents whole with their dates and authors, shifting from write-time distillation to read-time selection, enabling time-point-aware question answering over decision versions.
